title: Self-repair saga for Private VPC: terraform sentinels, canary upgrades, and automated remediation
creator: Aisha Moreno
description: Problem: Private (VPC) customer nodes occasionally fail periodic health probes (control-plane probes, agent heartbeats, storage attach checks) after upgrades or transient networking events. Existing alerts are noisy and current remediation is manual and slow. Goal: Ship a robust, auditable runbook plus an automated remediation pipeline that uses Terraform sentinel tags, a quarantine node pool, canary-aware upgrade hooks, and safe rollback criteria. This ticket collects the runbook, automation design, example terraform modules, and acceptance test plan.
acceptance_criteria: Health-check alert→automated remediation kicks off within 90s for qualifying failures
Automated repair success rate >= 95% across synthetic failure tests (runbook e2e harness)
False-positive rate on remediation trigger < 2% during a 2-week canary
All automated operations are recorded in the audit log with terraform plan/apply diffs and operator IDs
Canary upgrade flow drains ≤ 2% of production tokens per minute and preserves latency SLOs
proposed_solution: Introduce two complementary systems: 1) Terraform Sentinels: a small set of IaC modules and tag-based guards that mark instances as 'quarantined' and allow safe replacement via terraform without human SSH; 2) 'Self-Repair Saga' orchestrator: an idempotent controller (K8s job or Lambda) that consumes health-failure events, runs a deterministic sequence (isolate -> repair -> test -> rejoin) and emits detailed events to the Console and audit logs. Integrate canary gates in upgrade pipelines so the automations run in a staged fashion during post-upgrade windows.
automated_flow: 1) Alert ingestion: Cloud-monitoring alert (probe-failure) creates an event in the incidents topic with tags {node_id, failure_type, timestamp}
2) Triage filter: orchestration checks suppression rules (recent successful repair, scheduled maintenance window, golden-tags); if suppressed, record and stop
3) Sentinel tag: if unsuppressed, terraform sentinel module sets tf_tag=quarantined on the instance (terraform plan -> apply recorded)
4) Traffic isolation: orchestration calls kube/drain or load-balancer API to stop routing new requests to the instance (graceful drain with 60s timeout)
5) Repair actions (parallelized safe attempts): a) restart agent / systemd; b) reattach volumes via cloud APIs; c) reprovision instance (terraform taint -> apply) if software repair fails
6) Smoke tests: run 3 smoke probes (control-plane handshake, KV cache load, small unbatched generation) and verify latency and correctness thresholds
7) Rejoin: remove quarantine tag, un-drain or re-add to load balancer, and emit success event; if failure after 3 repair attempts, mark for replacement by operator and escalate
8) Fallback routing: during mass failures, route traffic to warm standby pool and optionally to hosted fallback model for critical customers
manual_runbook_steps: Step 0 — Context: Read the last 24h of node metrics in Console (latency, error-rate, heartbeat-age)
Step 1 — Correlate: Open the alert in the incidents topic and cross-reference the tf instance_id and last terraform apply
Step 2 — Quick fix: try soft repair commands (restart inference-agent: systemctl restart redwood-agent) and wait 45s for heartbeat
Step 3 — Drain: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60; confirm pods moved

Step 4 — Terraform sentinel: run 'terraform plan -target=module.node_sentinel' and review the plan for quarantining markers, then 'terraform apply' to set sentinel tags (operator must attach run ID to plan)
Step 5 — Replace: if soft fix fails, 'terraform taint module.node[<index>]' then 'terraform apply' to let autoscaler create a replacement; monitor new node join events
Step 6 — Smoke: after rejoin, run smoke.sh <node_ip> (3 probes) and confirm HTTP 200 and probe latency <200ms
Step 7 — Unquarantine: remove sentinel tag via terraform and 'kubectl uncordon <node>'
Step 8 — Postmortem: attach logs, terraform plan/apply outputs, and timeline to the incident; if trending, open a follow-up ticket
diag_commands:
# Check last agent heartbeat
curl -sS http://console.internal/api/nodes/<node_id>/heartbeat | jq .

# Restart agent
ssh ubuntu@<node_ip> 'sudo systemctl restart redwood-agent && sudo journalctl -u redwood-agent -n 200 --no-pager'

# Terraform plan for sentinel
cd infra/private && terraform init && terraform plan -target=module.node_sentinel -var 'run_id=<INCIDENT_ID>'

# Terraform taint + apply
terraform taint module.node[<index>] && terraform apply -auto-approve
rollback_strategy: If an automated repair causes regression (increase in error-rate or latency beyond SLO within 10 minutes), the orchestrator will revert the last terraform apply using saved state snapshot (terraform state rollback) and re-mark the instance as quarantined. For upgrades, canary gate automatically pauses pipeline and re-runs previous stable revision. Emergency operator command 'redwood-repair abort <run_id>' will stop automation and open an operator review ticket.
notes: We must avoid automated tainting during maintenance windows — maintenance windows are published to the incidents topic and respected by the triage filter.
Auditability: every terraform plan/apply invoked by automation must include the orchestration run_id and operator identity header so we can reproduce postmortems.

During initial canary (2 weeks), the automation will only auto-repair non-network failures; network failures will create an event but require manual approval to proceed. This reduces blast radius while validating logic.
Consider adding a 'cost guard' to avoid repeated reprovision loops that could create new instances in expensive AZs.
risk_assessment: Medium-High: Automation reduces MTTR but increases the blast radius if the detection logic has a bug. Mitigations: staged canaries, strict suppression rules, operator opt-in for high-risk failure classes, and immutable audit logs for every terraform change. Rollback hooks and warm-standby routing reduce user-visible impact.
